strongest_angle: Global critical mineral risk is driven less by broad geopolitical blocs like BRICS versus the West and more by physical refining chokepoints where individual ports or processing facilities control entire supply chains.

key_facts.fact: China currently leads the refining process across 19 out of 20 strategic critical minerals, making physical processing facilities the primary global supply chokepoint.
During his 1992 Southern Tour in the Inner Mongolia Baotou rare-earth basin, leader Deng Xiaoping explicitly declared that China has rare earths just as the Middle East has oil.
The Center for Strategic and International Studies notes that the primary strategic objective for the United States in critical minerals policy is reducing reliance on Chinese processing capacity.
key_facts.source_name: Center for Strategic and International Studies
